subproblem.title: Countable family uniformly approximating C_c(X) with support control (X locally compact, Hausdorff, second countable)
subproblem.statement: Let X be a locally compact Hausdorff topological space with a countable basis. Then there is a sequence (g_k)_{k∈ℕ} of continuous compactly supported functions g_k : X → ℝ such that for every continuous compactly supported f : X → ℝ there is a compact set K ⊆ X with tsupport f ⊆ K such that for every η > 0 there is k ∈ ℕ with tsupport g_k ⊆ K and |f(x) − g_k(x)| ≤ η for all x ∈ X.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [LocallyCompactSpace X] [SecondCountableTopology X], ∃ g : ℕ → C_c(X, ℝ), ∀ f : C_c(X, ℝ), ∃ K : Set X, IsCompact K ∧ tsupport f ⊆ K ∧ ∀ η : ℝ, 0 < η → ∃ k : ℕ, tsupport (g k) ⊆ K ∧ ∀ x : X, |f x - g k x| ≤ η
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. This is the "countable dense family" step (step 2) of the parent proof, i.e. the erratum-corrected form of the Alaoglu step in Simon's printed proof of Ch. 1, Theorem 4.16 (p. 37): "Let K_1, K_2, ... be an increasing sequence of compact sets with X = ∪_j K_j and let F_{j,k} : C(K_j) → ℝ be defined by F_{j,k}(f) = ∫_{K_j} f dμ_k, k = 1, 2, .... By the Alaoglu theorem there is a subsequence F_{j,k'} and a non-negative bounded functional F_j : C(K_j) → ℝ with F_{j,k'}(f) → F_j(f) for each f ∈ C(K_j)." ERRATUM (GMT/Ch01/README.md; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_4_16_counterexample): the Alaoglu theorem only yields a subnet, not a subsequence; for second-countable X the step is made sequential by testing against a countable family of test functions which approximates every test function uniformly, with supports inside one compact set that depends only on the approximated function. This lemma constructs that family, for a general locally compact, Hausdorff, second-countable X (the parent applies it to the open subset U × G(N,n) of ℝ^N × G(N,n), as a subtype). It is step 1 (compact exhaustion) and step 2 (cutoff times countable dense family) of the parent proof of varifold_radon_compactness; instead of a countable dense subset of each C(X_{m+1}) in the sup norm, one countable dense subset of C(X,ℝ) for the compact-open topology (= uniform convergence on compact sets) is used, which serves all m at once.

Throughout, X is locally compact, Hausdorff and second countable; C_c(X,ℝ) is the set of continuous f : X → ℝ with compact topological support tsupport f = closure{f ≠ 0}.

1. Compact exhaustion. A locally compact second-countable space is σ-compact (Mathlib instance sigmaCompactSpace_of_locallyCompact_secondCountable). Hence there are compact sets E_0 ⊆ E_1 ⊆ E_2 ⊆ ... with E_m ⊆ interior(E_{m+1}) for every m and ⋃_m E_m = X (Mathlib: E := CompactExhaustion.choice X, with E.isCompact, E.subset_interior_succ, E.subset_succ). Moreover every compact C ⊆ X lies in some E_m (E.exists_superset_of_isCompact): the open sets interior(E_{m+1}) increase with m and cover X (each x lies in some E_m ⊆ interior(E_{m+1})), so finitely many of them, hence a single one, cover C, and interior(E_{m+1}) ⊆ E_{m+1}.

2. Cutoff functions. X is locally compact and Hausdorff, hence regular. Fix m. The set E_m is compact, the set (interior E_{m+1})ᶜ is closed, and they are disjoint because E_m ⊆ interior(E_{m+1}). By Urysohn's lemma for locally compact regular spaces (Mathlib exists_continuous_one_zero_of_isCompact) there is a continuous χ_m : X → ℝ with χ_m = 1 on E_m, χ_m = 0 on X ∖ interior(E_{m+1}), χ_m of compact support, and 0 ≤ χ_m(x) ≤ 1 for all x. Then {χ_m ≠ 0} ⊆ interior(E_{m+1}) ⊆ E_{m+1}, and E_{m+1} is closed (compact in a Hausdorff space), so tsupport χ_m ⊆ E_{m+1}; in particular χ_m(x) = 0 for x ∉ E_{m+1}.

3. A countable dense subset of C(X,ℝ). Equip the space C(X,ℝ) of continuous real functions with the compact-open topology. Since X is locally compact and second countable and ℝ is second countable, C(X,ℝ) is second countable, hence separable (Mathlib ContinuousMap.instSecondCountableTopology / ContinuousMap.instSeparableSpace, in the module Mathlib.Topology.ContinuousMap.SecondCountableSpace, which the Lean proof must import). As C(X,ℝ) is nonempty (it contains 0), there is a sequence (d_i)_{i∈ℕ} in C(X,ℝ) with dense range (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.denseSeq, denseRange_denseSeq). The compact-open topology of C(X,ℝ) is the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets: it is the topology of the compact-convergence uniformity, which has the basis of entourages {(h,h') : ∀ x ∈ L, (h(x), h'(x)) ∈ W} with L ⊆ X compact and W an entourage of ℝ (Mathlib ContinuousMap.compactConvergenceUniformSpace, ContinuousMap.hasBasis_compactConvergenceUniformity). Consequently, for every h ∈ C(X,ℝ), every compact L ⊆ X and every η > 0 the set {h' ∈ C(X,ℝ) : |h(x) − h'(x)| < η for all x ∈ L} is a neighbourhood of h (it is the ball around h for the entourage obtained from L and W = {(s,t) : |s − t| < η}; UniformSpace.ball_mem_nhds), so by density (Dense.inter_nhds_nonempty) it contains some d_i.

4. The family. Let ℕ → ℕ × ℕ, k ↦ (m(k), i(k)) := Nat.unpair k, be the standard bijection, with inverse (m, i) ↦ Nat.pair m i. Define g_k := χ_{m(k)} · d_{i(k)} (pointwise product). It is continuous, and it has compact support because χ_{m(k)} does (HasCompactSupport.mul_right); so g_k ∈ C_c(X,ℝ). Moreover tsupport g_k ⊆ tsupport χ_{m(k)} ⊆ E_{m(k)+1} (tsupport_mul_subset_left and step 2).

5. The approximation property. Let f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ). Since tsupport f is compact, step 1 gives m with tsupport f ⊆ E_m. Put K := E_{m+1}. Then K is compact and tsupport f ⊆ E_m ⊆ E_{m+1} = K. Now let η > 0. By step 3, applied to h = f (regarded as an element of C(X,ℝ)), L = E_{m+1} and η, there is i with |f(x) − d_i(x)| < η for all x ∈ E_{m+1}. Let k := Nat.pair m i; then (m(k), i(k)) = (m, i), so g_k = χ_m · d_i and, by step 4, tsupport g_k ⊆ E_{m+1} = K. It remains to show |f(x) − g_k(x)| ≤ η for every x ∈ X.
 (a) f(x) = χ_m(x) f(x) for every x: if x ∈ E_m then χ_m(x) = 1; if x ∉ E_m then x ∉ tsupport f (as tsupport f ⊆ E_m), so f(x) = 0 and both sides vanish.
 (b) Hence f(x) − g_k(x) = χ_m(x) f(x) − χ_m(x) d_i(x) = χ_m(x)(f(x) − d_i(x)), and since χ_m(x) ≥ 0, |f(x) − g_k(x)| = χ_m(x) |f(x) − d_i(x)|.
 (c) If x ∈ E_{m+1}, then |f(x) − d_i(x)| < η and 0 ≤ χ_m(x) ≤ 1, so |f(x) − g_k(x)| ≤ 1 · η = η.
 (d) If x ∉ E_{m+1}, then χ_m(x) = 0 by step 2, so |f(x) − g_k(x)| = 0 ≤ η (as η > 0).
Thus g = (g_k)_k has the required property: for every f the compact set K = E_{m+1} contains tsupport f, and for every η > 0 the index k = Nat.pair m i satisfies tsupport g_k ⊆ K and |f(x) − g_k(x)| ≤ η for all x. (If X is empty, all statements hold trivially and the same construction applies.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Compact exhaustion E_m of X (σ-compact since locally compact and second countable): E_m ⊆ interior E_{m+1}, every compact set lies in some E_m.
Urysohn cutoffs χ_m ∈ C_c(X): χ_m = 1 on E_m, 0 ≤ χ_m ≤ 1, tsupport χ_m ⊆ E_{m+1}.
C(X,ℝ) with the compact-open topology (= uniform convergence on compacts) is second countable, hence has a dense sequence d_i (needs import Mathlib.Topology.ContinuousMap.SecondCountableSpace).
g_{Nat.pair m i} := χ_m · d_i ∈ C_c(X,ℝ) with tsupport ⊆ E_{m+1}.
For tsupport f ⊆ E_m take K = E_{m+1}: f = χ_m f, so |f − χ_m d_i| = χ_m |f − d_i| ≤ η when sup_{E_{m+1}} |f − d_i| < η.

audit.reason: The prose includes every hypothesis and matches the standalone one-line Lean proposition. Compact exhaustion, Urysohn cutoffs and compact-open separability provide the stated sequence. The fixed compact K depends only on f, and the pointwise estimate holds both inside and outside K, including empty X. The proof is complete and non-circular. The fresh bare name is valid; the additional separability import is permitted.

subproblem.title: Riesz representation of the vague limit functional (final step of Simon 4.16 via Theorem 4.12)
subproblem.statement: Let X be a locally compact Hausdorff space with its Borel σ-algebra and μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) measures on X such that for every compact K ⊆ X there is C_K < ∞ with μ_j(K) ≤ C_K for all sufficiently large j, and such that for every continuous compactly supported f : X → ℝ the real sequence (∫ f dμ_j)_j converges. Then there is a locally finite measure ν on X with ∫ f dμ_j → ∫ f dν for every continuous compactly supported f : X → ℝ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [LocallyCompactSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (μ : ℕ → Measure X), (∀ K : Set X, IsCompact K → ∃ C : ℝ≥0∞, C ≠ ∞ ∧ ∀ᶠ j in atTop, μ j K ≤ C) → (∀ f : C_c(X, ℝ), ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun j ↦ ∫ x, f x ∂(μ j)) atTop (𝓝 L)) → ∃ ν : Measure X, IsLocallyFiniteMeasure ν ∧ ∀ f : C_c(X, ℝ), Tendsto (fun j ↦ ∫ x, f x ∂(μ j)) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, f x ∂ν))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 1, printed proof of Theorem 4.16 (pp. 37–38), last part: "... we then get a subsequence μ_{k'} and a non-negative linear F : K(X) → ℝ with ∫_X f dμ_{k'} → F(f) for each f ∈ K(X) ... Then by applying Theorem 4.12 we have a Radon measure μ on X such that F(f) = ∫_X f dμ for each f ∈ K(X), and so ∫_X f dμ_{k'} → ∫_X f dμ for each f ∈ K(X)." This is step 4 (linearity and positivity of the limit functional F) and step 5 (Riesz representation) of the parent proof of varifold_radon_compactness, stated for a general locally compact Hausdorff space X with its Borel σ-algebra; the sequence here plays the role of the already extracted subsequence. No erratum affects this part (second countability is not needed for it). The mass bounds are assumed only for all sufficiently large j, which is all that is used.

Throughout, X is locally compact Hausdorff with its Borel σ-algebra, μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) are measures on X such that for every compact K ⊆ X there are C_K ∈ [0,∞) and J_K with μ_j(K) ≤ C_K for j ≥ J_K, and for every f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ) the real sequence (∫ f dμ_j)_j converges. Integrals are Bochner integrals (0 for non-integrable functions).

1. Eventual integrability. Let f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ) and K := tsupport f, a compact set. Choose C_K, J_K as above. For j ≥ J_K we have μ_j(K) ≤ C_K < ∞. The function f is continuous, hence a.e.-strongly measurable for μ_j (X is Borel and ℝ is second countable), and bounded: |f(x)| ≤ M for all x for some M (continuous with compact support). Hence f is μ_j-integrable on K (bounded measurable function on a set of finite measure; Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded), and because f = 0 outside K (support f ⊆ tsupport f = K), f is μ_j-integrable on X (integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset). Thus: for every f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ), f is μ_j-integrable for all sufficiently large j.

2. The limit functional. For f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ) let F(f) ∈ ℝ be the limit of (∫ f dμ_j)_j, which exists by hypothesis and is unique because ℝ is Hausdorff (in Lean: F(f) := limUnder atTop (fun j ↦ ∫ f dμ_j), with tendsto_nhds_limUnder).
 (a) Additivity. Let f, g ∈ C_c(X,ℝ). By step 1 there is J such that f and g are μ_j-integrable for all j ≥ J, and for those j, ∫ (f + g) dμ_j = ∫ f dμ_j + ∫ g dμ_j (integral_add). The right-hand side tends to F(f) + F(g); hence (∫ (f + g) dμ_j)_j, which agrees with it for j ≥ J, also tends to F(f) + F(g) (Tendsto.congr'), and by uniqueness of limits (tendsto_nhds_unique) F(f + g) = F(f) + F(g).
 (b) Homogeneity. Let c ∈ ℝ and f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ). For every j, ∫ c f dμ_j = c ∫ f dμ_j (integral_const_mul; this holds without any integrability assumption). The right side tends to c F(f), so F(c f) = c F(f).
 (c) Positivity. If f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ) satisfies f(x) ≥ 0 for all x, then ∫ f dμ_j ≥ 0 for every j (integral_nonneg), so the limit satisfies F(f) ≥ 0 (ge_of_tendsto').
 Hence F is a positive linear functional on C_c(X,ℝ) (in Lean: the linear map of (a)–(b) packaged by PositiveLinearMap.mk₀ with (c), giving F : C_c(X,ℝ) →ₚ[ℝ] ℝ).

3. Riesz representation (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 4.12; Mathlib's real Riesz–Markov–Kakutani theorem). Since X is locally compact Hausdorff with its Borel σ-algebra, ν := RealRMK.rieszMeasure F is a measure on X with ∫ f dν = F(f) for every f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ) (RealRMK.integral_rieszMeasure). The measure ν is regular (RealRMK.regular_rieszMeasure); a regular measure is finite on compact sets, and on a locally compact space a measure that is finite on compact sets is locally finite, because every point has a compact neighbourhood (Mathlib instance isLocallyFiniteMeasure_of_isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts). So ν is locally finite.

4. Conclusion. For every f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ), ∫ f dμ_j → F(f) = ∫ f dν as j → ∞. Together with step 3 this gives the required locally finite measure ν. ∎
proof_key_steps: Each f ∈ C_c(X) is μ_j-integrable for all large j (bounded, supported in the compact tsupport f of eventually finite mass).
F(f) := lim_j ∫ f dμ_j is additive (eventual integrability + uniqueness of limits), homogeneous and positive, i.e. a positive linear functional on C_c(X,ℝ).
Riesz–Markov–Kakutani (RealRMK.rieszMeasure, integral_rieszMeasure): ν with ∫ f dν = F(f); ν is regular, hence finite on compacts, hence locally finite on the locally compact X.
∫ f dμ_j → F(f) = ∫ f dν for every f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ).

subproblem.title: Diagonal subsequence along which ∫ f dμ_j converges for every f ∈ C_c(X) (sequential, erratum-corrected Alaoglu step of Simon 4.16)
subproblem.statement: Let X be a locally compact Hausdorff second-countable space with its Borel σ-algebra and μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) measures on X such that for every compact K ⊆ X there is C_K < ∞ with μ_j(K) ≤ C_K for all sufficiently large j. Then there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that for every continuous compactly supported f : X → ℝ the real sequence (∫ f dμ_{φ(j)})_{j∈ℕ} converges.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [LocallyCompactSpace X] [SecondCountableTopology X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (μ : ℕ → Measure X), (∀ K : Set X, IsCompact K → ∃ C : ℝ≥0∞, C ≠ ∞ ∧ ∀ᶠ j in atTop, μ j K ≤ C) → ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ f : C_c(X, ℝ), ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun j ↦ ∫ x, f x ∂(μ (φ j))) atTop (𝓝 L)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 1, printed proof of Theorem 4.16 (p. 37): "By the Alaoglu theorem there is a subsequence F_{j,k'} and a non-negative bounded functional F_j : C(K_j) → ℝ with F_{j,k'}(f) → F_j(f) for each f ∈ C(K_j). By choosing the subsequences successively and taking a diagonal sequence, we then get a subsequence μ_{k'} and a non-negative linear F : K(X) → ℝ with ∫_X f dμ_{k'} → F(f) for each f ∈ K(X)". ERRATUM (GMT/Ch01/README.md; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_4_16_counterexample): as printed (X only locally compact, σ-compact, Hausdorff) this is false, because the Alaoglu step yields a subnet and not a subsequence; for second-countable X the step is made sequential exactly as in steps 3–4 of the parent proof: extract a diagonal subsequence along a countable family of test functions (the sibling lemma radon_compactlySupported_countable_approx) and extend to all test functions by uniform approximation and the local mass bounds. Second (immaterial) adaptation, as in the parent: the mass bounds are only assumed for all sufficiently large j (finitely many μ_j may have infinite mass on K). This lemma is steps 3–4 of the parent proof of varifold_radon_compactness, for a general locally compact, Hausdorff, second-countable X with its Borel σ-algebra.

Notation. For a measure ν and f : X → ℝ, ∫ f dν is the Bochner integral (it is 0 by convention when f is not ν-integrable; every estimate below is used only for indices at which integrability has been verified, or is valid without integrability). For a compact (hence closed, hence Borel) set K and a measure ν with ν(K) < ∞ write ν(K) also for the real number (ν K).toReal.

0. Two elementary facts.
 (a) Integrability. Let h ∈ C_c(X,ℝ), K ⊆ X a compact set with tsupport h ⊆ K, and ν a measure on X with ν(K) < ∞. Then h is ν-integrable. Indeed h is continuous, hence (X Borel, ℝ second countable) a.e.-strongly measurable for ν; h is bounded, |h(x)| ≤ M for all x, since it is continuous with compact support (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support); so h is integrable on K (a bounded measurable function on a set of finite measure; Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded), and since h = 0 outside K (support h ⊆ tsupport h ⊆ K) it is integrable on X (integrableOn_iff_integrable_of_support_subset).
 (b) Estimate. Let K ⊆ X be compact, ν a measure with ν(K) < ∞, η ≥ 0 a real number and h : X → ℝ with h(x) = 0 for x ∉ K and |h(x)| ≤ η for all x. Then |∫ h dν| ≤ η ν(K). Indeed ∫ h dν = ∫_K h dν because h vanishes off K (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero), and |∫_K h dν| ≤ η ν(K) (norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const).

1. The countable family. By the sibling lemma radon_compactlySupported_countable_approx (X is locally compact, Hausdorff, second countable) there is a sequence (g_k)_{k∈ℕ} in C_c(X,ℝ) such that for every f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ) there is a compact K_f ⊆ X with tsupport f ⊆ K_f and, for every η > 0, some k with tsupport g_k ⊆ K_f and |f(x) − g_k(x)| ≤ η for all x ∈ X.

2. Each sequence a_k(j) := ∫ g_k dμ_j (j ∈ ℕ) is bounded. Fix k and let T_k := tsupport g_k, a compact set. By hypothesis there are C_k ∈ [0,∞) and J_k ∈ ℕ with μ_j(T_k) ≤ C_k for all j ≥ J_k; write c_k := C_k as a real number (c_k ≥ 0). Choose M_k ∈ ℝ with |g_k(x)| ≤ M_k for all x (0(a)); then also |g_k(x)| ≤ |M_k|. For j ≥ J_k we have μ_j(T_k) ≤ C_k < ∞, so by 0(b) (with h = g_k, K = T_k, η = |M_k|) |a_k(j)| ≤ |M_k| μ_j(T_k) ≤ |M_k| c_k. Put B_k := |M_k| c_k + Σ_{j < J_k} |a_k(j)|. Then |a_k(j)| ≤ B_k for every j ∈ ℕ: if j ≥ J_k this follows from the previous estimate because the finite sum is ≥ 0; if j < J_k, then |a_k(j)| is one of the nonnegative summands of Σ_{j' < J_k} |a_k(j')| and |M_k| c_k ≥ 0.

3. Diagonal extraction (the sequential form of "choosing the subsequences successively and taking a diagonal sequence"). Consider the space ℝ^ℕ of real sequences with the product topology and its points A_j := (a_k(j))_{k∈ℕ}, j ∈ ℕ. By step 2 every A_j lies in P := ∏_{k∈ℕ} [−B_k, B_k], which is compact by Tychonoff's theorem (Mathlib isCompact_univ_pi with isCompact_Icc). The space ℝ^ℕ is first countable (a countable product of first-countable spaces; it is even metrizable), so the compact set P is sequentially compact (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq): there are a = (a_k)_k ∈ P and a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with A_{φ(j)} → a in ℝ^ℕ as j → ∞. Convergence in the product topology is coordinatewise convergence (tendsto_pi_nhds), so for every k: ∫ g_k dμ_{φ(j)} = a_k(φ(j)) → a_k as j → ∞. In particular every sequence (a_k(φ(j)))_j is a Cauchy sequence.

4. Convergence for every test function. Let f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ), and let K := K_f be the compact set of step 1, so tsupport f ⊆ K. By hypothesis there are C ∈ [0,∞) and J ∈ ℕ with μ_j(K) ≤ C for all j ≥ J; let c := C as a real number, c ≥ 0. We prove that (∫ f dμ_{φ(j)})_{j∈ℕ} is a Cauchy sequence of reals. Let ε > 0 and put η := ε/(2c + 2) > 0, so that η(2c + 2) = ε. By step 1 choose k with tsupport g_k ⊆ K and |f(x) − g_k(x)| ≤ η for all x. By step 3 choose N_1 with |a_k(φ(p)) − a_k(φ(q))| < η for all p, q ≥ N_1.
 (i) For every p ≥ J: since φ is strictly increasing, φ(p) ≥ p ≥ J, so μ_{φ(p)}(K) ≤ C < ∞. By 0(a), f and g_k are μ_{φ(p)}-integrable (both have topological support in K), hence ∫ f dμ_{φ(p)} − ∫ g_k dμ_{φ(p)} = ∫ (f − g_k) dμ_{φ(p)}. The function f − g_k vanishes outside K (both f and g_k vanish outside their topological supports, which lie in K) and |f − g_k| ≤ η, so by 0(b) |∫ f dμ_{φ(p)} − a_k(φ(p))| ≤ η μ_{φ(p)}(K) ≤ η c.
 (ii) For p, q ≥ N := max(N_1, J), by the triangle inequality and (i),
 |∫ f dμ_{φ(p)} − ∫ f dμ_{φ(q)}| ≤ |∫ f dμ_{φ(p)} − a_k(φ(p))| + |a_k(φ(p)) − a_k(φ(q))| + |a_k(φ(q)) − ∫ f dμ_{φ(q)}| < ηc + η + ηc ≤ η(2c + 2) = ε.
 Hence the sequence is Cauchy (Metric.cauchySeq_iff), and since ℝ is complete it converges to some L ∈ ℝ (cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete).
Since φ was chosen in step 3 independently of f, the strictly increasing φ works for every f ∈ C_c(X,ℝ) simultaneously, which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Countable approximating family g_k from the sibling lemma radon_compactlySupported_countable_approx.
Each sequence (∫ g_k dμ_j)_j is bounded: eventual bound |M_k|·C_k plus the finitely many initial terms.
Tychonoff: ∏_k [−B_k, B_k] ⊆ ℝ^ℕ is compact and ℝ^ℕ is first countable, so a subsequence φ makes every ∫ g_k dμ_{φ(j)} converge (diagonal step).
For f ∈ C_c(X): approximate uniformly by g_k supported in K_f, use the eventual mass bound on K_f and φ(p) ≥ p to get a Cauchy sequence, hence a limit in ℝ.

audit.reason: The prose and exact Lean type agree, including eventual rather than uniform-in-index bounds. Finite initial Bochner integral values are correctly absorbed into coordinate bounds. Compactness and first countability of the countable product yield a common strictly increasing subsequence. Eventual integrability and support-controlled approximation justify the Cauchy estimate for every test function. Its sole dependency on cc_countable_approx is correctly directed and acyclic; the bare name is fresh.
